content.text:
The fix never landed. Your saved setting still says `"isUndetectable": true`, and that file hasn't been written since May 27. Neither the in-app switch nor the terminal command reached it, so content protection is still on and Zoom still gets the black box.

I checked the code behind that switch and it's wired correctly: flipping it turns protection off on every window right away and saves the change. So most likely the switch got clicked twice (on, then back on), or it was flipped in a different copy of the app than the one you run in meetings.

My sandbox still can't write to `~/Library`, so here's the surest way to fix it from your terminal:

1. Quit Natively completely (Cmd+Q, or quit it from the menu bar icon). If it's still running when you save the file, it can write `true` back.
2. Run:
   ```
   sed -i '' 's/"isUndetectable": true/"isUndetectable": false/' ~/Library/Application\ Support/natively/settings.json && cat ~/Library/Application\ Support/natively/settings.json
   ```
   The printout should now say `"isUndetectable": false`.
3. Reopen the app, open Settings, and make sure the label reads "Natively is currently detectable by screen-sharing."
4. In Zoom, stop sharing and start again. Zoom keeps showing the old black frame for a window until you restart the share.

If it's still a black box after that, tell me two things and I'll dig further: what the printout in step 2 shows, and whether you share your whole screen or just one window. And if "not working properly" means something other than the black box, tell me what you're seeing.

status_detail: saved setting still true; sandbox can't write ~/Library
needs_action: quit Natively fully, then run the step 2 sed command in your terminal
